Autumn entered the valley like a thief with exquisite taste, stealing only the green and leaving behind a ransacked treasury of amber, vermillion, and burnt sienna. The trees wore their dying like finery. They had no shame about it... this annual rehearsal for disappearance. The children walked to school through corridors of falling leaves and did not notice the beauty, because children are themselves a kind of beauty and cannot see their own reflection in the world. An old man sat on a bench near the courthouse and watched them pass. He remembered being that small. He remembered when autumn was merely a season and not a metaphor for everything he had become. The wind moved through the square, rearranging the leaves into patterns that almost meant something... hieroglyphs of chance, scripture written by indifference. He pulled his coat tighter. The cold was arriving early this year, punctual as grief.
